  "headline": "Established the browser game outcome, server and test requirements, and intake defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Outcome: a small browser-playable Battleship game for one person against the computer, usable through the game’s browser entry point. Fact: no deployment target, earlier run, team, workspace, channel, internal site, document, private repository or owner is named; there are no source hints to pursue beyond the request and available workspace. Recorded defaults: use familiar Battleship rules, with the player placing a fleet, taking turns with the computer and seeing a win or loss; identify the player by an anonymous game session; keep each game separate and in memory for that session, ending it on completion or restart; hide the computer’s unhit ships from the player and prevent the computer from using hidden player-ship information to choose shots. These defaults rule out accounts, shared or cross-device games, and recovery after the session or server ends. Open interaction question: discovery must first establish what the browser and server runtime already provide for sessions and state; discovery then chooses how to identify the session and preserve the stated visibility boundaries, which blocks implementation of game state and interactions. S2 — Outcome: a Node.js server and tests covering the game’s behavior. Fact: the repository is empty and no existing test framework or runtime facilities are specified; discovery must establish the available Node.js environment before choosing the test setup, which blocks implementation and test execution. Boundary: this stage implements nothing; in the isolated run, the source checkout remains at its snapshot until the final return, when the completed source and tests can become visible there. The game becomes playable after the returned server is started and opened in a browser; a deployed outcome exists only after release."
}
